question.text: A wooden cylinder of mass <math> <mrow> <mtext>20 g</mtext></mrow> </math> and area of cross-section <math> <mrow> <mtext>1</mtext><mtext> </mtext><msup> <mrow> <mtext>cm</mtext></mrow> <mn>2</mn> </msup> </mrow> </math>, having a piece of lead of mass <math> <mrow> <mn>60</mn><mtext> </mtext><mtext>g</mtext></mrow> </math> attached to its bottom, floats in water. The cylinder is depressed and then released. The frequency of oscillations is <!-- MathType@Translator@5@5@MathML2 (namespace attr).tdl@MathML 2.0 (namespace attr)@ --> <math> <mrow> <mfrac> <mtext>N</mtext> <mtext>π</mtext> </mfrac> <msup> <mn>s</mn> <mrow> <mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>. Find the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>N</mi></math>. [Neglect the volume of water displaced by the lead piece, take <!-- MathType@Translator@5@5@MathML2 (namespace attr).tdl@MathML 2.0 (namespace attr)@ --> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9.8</mn><mtext> </mtext><msup><mtext>m/s</mtext><mtext>2</mtext></msup></math>, density of water <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">w</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>cm</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math>]<!-- MathType@End@5@5@ -->

solution.text:
Suppose that the loaded wooden block sinks upto a height h. Then,

weight of water displaced by the block

= weight of the block with lead

If a is area of cross-section of the block and σ, the density of water, then

a h⁡ σ g = M + m g

or h⁡ = M + m a σ

= 2 0 + 6 0 1 × 1 = 8 0 cm ∵ density of water = 1gcm - 3

Now for small displacement ' x' from equilibrium

σga( x+h )−( M+m )g=-( M+m )A

σgax=-( M+m )A

A=- σga M+m x

f= 1 2π g h

= 1 2π 980 80   = 1.75 π s −1
